text: Parents challenged Katherine Paterson's Bridge to Terabithia in 1986 as recommended reading for 6th grade students in the Lincoln, NE schools, objecting to its “profanity,” including “Oh, Lord” and the use of “Lord” as an expletive. In Coweta County, objections to the book and others used in elementary classrooms and available in school libraries cited profanity, the mention of ghosts, and a reference to an attempted rape; removal was requested, but school and county review committees retained it for classroom and library use while restricting it to middle school classrooms. In Marshalltown, an objector requested its removal from a fifth-grade literature class over profanity; after the objector failed to attend a scheduled hearing, the book was not withdrawn from the curriculum.
meta_description: Bridge to Terabithia by Katherine Paterson: challenged in Lincoln, NE in 1986 over profanity; retained in Coweta County and Marshalltown.
